result.topic_en: Euler derives the two Euler–Lagrange-type differential equations (one for y and one for z as functions of x) that a space curve not lying in one plane must satisfy to possess a maximum or minimum property.
result.transcription:
22
per methodum ordinariam facile expediri poterit. Cum
enim nunc $z$ tanquam certa functio ipsius $x$ spectari pos-
sit, etiam quantitates inde derivatae tanquam tales functio-
nes spectari poterunt, unde in valore differentiali pro $\partial V$
assumto omnes hi termini:
$N'\partial z + P'\partial p' + Q'\partial q' + R'\partial r'$ etc.
jam in membro $M dx$ contineri erunt censendi; quare cum
littera $M$ in aequationem finalem non ingrediatur, aequa-
tio inter $x$ et $y$ hac exprimetur aequatione:
$N - \frac{\partial P}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial\partial Q}{\partial x^2} - \frac{\partial^3 R}{\partial x^2} = o.$

8. Quodsi jam simili modo valorem ipsius $y$, quasi
jam esset cognitus, contemplemur, ita ut tam $y$ quam
$p$, $q$, $r$ tanquam functiones cognitae ipsius $x$ spectari
queant, hi termini: $N\partial y + P\partial p + Q\partial q + R\partial r$, ad for-
mam $M\partial x$ accedere erunt censendi, sicque aequatio inter
$z$ et $x$ per hanc aequationem definietur:
$N' - \frac{\partial P'}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial\partial Q}{\partial x^2} - \frac{\partial^3 R}{\partial x^3} = o.$

9. Ex his conjunctis manifesto sequitur, si neutra
harum aequationum tanquam cognita spectari queat, sed
utraque definiri debeat, quaesito satisfieri his binis aequa-
tionibus conjungendis:
I. $N - \frac{\partial P}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial\partial Q}{\partial x^2} - \frac{\partial^3 R}{\partial x^3} = o$,
II. $N' - \frac{\partial P'}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial\partial Q'}{\partial x^2} - \frac{\partial^3 R'}{\partial x^3} = o$,

$N - \frac{\partial P}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial\partial Q}{\partial x^2} - \frac{\partial^3 R}{\partial x^2} = o.$
items.english: The equation between x and y will be expressed by this equation: N - dP/dx + d²Q/dx² - d³R/dx³ = 0.

items.quote:

$z$ et $x$ per hanc aequationem definietur:
$N' - \frac{\partial P'}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial\partial Q}{\partial x^2} - \frac{\partial^3 R}{\partial x^3} = o.$
items.english: And thus the equation between z and x will be defined by this equation: N' - dP'/dx + d²Q'/dx² - d³R'/dx³ = 0.

items.quote:
Ex his conjunctis manifesto sequitur, si neutra

items.english: From these combined it manifestly follows that, if neither of these equations can be regarded as known but both must be determined, the problem is satisfied by joining these two equations together.
